subtype: Helping together at school or in a colony [Actor]
passage:
Friday. Chandrika noticed the colony park was full of wrappers and old bottles. She told her friends on the swings. “Who will clean it?” asked Hrithik. “We will,” she said.
Saturday. Six children turned up with gloves and cloth bags. Two uncles brought sacks and showed them how to separate plastic. Hrithik carried the heaviest bag and puffed. A small boy named Anand held the bag open with both hands, silent and proud.
Sunday. The park looked different. A little girl swung on the swings and laughed. Chandrika stood at the gate and grinned. “We did that,” she said quietly.

qa.q: How many children came to clean the park on Saturday?
qa.a: Six children turned up with gloves and cloth bags.

qa.q: How did Chandrika feel on Sunday when she saw the clean park?
qa.a: Chandrika felt proud. Standing at the gate and grinning, she quietly said that they had done it.

qa.q: What small step turned Chandrika's noticing into action?
qa.a: When Hrithik asked who would clean it, she said “we will” and invited her friends. That made it a shared job, not a complaint.

qa.q: How might Anand, who held the bag open, have felt?
qa.a: Anand probably felt proud to have a real job in the clean-up, since he held the bag with both hands, silent and proud.

grounding: Shows a child joining a clean-up drive with friends and feeling proud that together they made a difference.

subtype: Helping together at school or in a colony [Actor]
passage:
Jahnavi, you asked why I keep this old school badge. Let me tell you. When I was ten, my class decided to collect used books for a village school. I’m Neelam, and I had never organised anything.
We borrowed a handcart. Ravi, the strongest boy, pulled it. A quiet girl, Divya, kept the list and ticked every house. I only knocked on doors and felt my knees shake.
By evening we had three hundred books. Our teacher looked at the cart and said nothing for a while. Then she smiled. Divya put her pencil behind her ear and we all laughed.

qa.a: Neelam's class collected used books for a village school.

qa.q: How might Neelam have felt knocking on doors?
qa.a: Neelam was nervous, since the knees shook. Neelam had never organised anything before but kept knocking on doors anyway.

qa.q: Which choice by the class made the collection succeed?
qa.a: They divided the jobs: Ravi pulled the cart, Divya kept the list and Neelam knocked on doors. Each child did the part that suited them.

qa.q: What might Divya have been feeling as she ticked every house on the list?
qa.a: Divya may have felt proud and focused, since her quiet job kept everyone's effort organised. Putting the pencil behind her ear at the end suggests a happy, satisfied mood.

grounding: An elder recalls a childhood book drive with a class, where each child's small part added up to something real.
